- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) but underperform in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3), especially after recent spikes.
- Overshoots occur after strong upward moves; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment drops or stabilizes below 0.6.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not exceed 10% above recent high.
- Lagged overreaction: if sentiment spikes but price doesn’t follow, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 3–5% for 2–3 days after sentiment peak.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising; adjust downward by 2–4% for first 7 days if sentiment > 0.7.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is low but price is high, don’t assume continuation; reduce forecast by 5–8% if sentiment < 0.3 and price > 75.00.
